author: RYAN SPOEHR
title: Political debate at Janesville Bus Terminal leads to fight: One man strikes a low blow, the other throws his belongings into Rock River - NewsBreak
text:
By RYAN SPOEHR ,
13 hours ago
JANESVILLE — A political debate at about 1 a.m. June 4 at the downtown Janesville Transit bus terminal turned violent to the point one man in the fight allegedly grabbed and twisted the other person’s genitalia in retaliation.
Another man had his backpack tossed in the Rock River during the fracas.
According to a criminal complaint, a man who was unidentified was laying down and was approached by someone else, later identified as Jonathyn J. Torgerson, Janesville, 31, who spoke about politics. The unidentified man reported that the conversation became heated and Torgerson started punching the other man in the face.
The man said he fought back, and “at one point bit the other subject on the arm and grabbed the subject’s genitals and twisted in order to get the subject off of him.”
Then, Torgerson took the man’s belongings, including a backpack, and threw them in the Rock River, according to the complaint. The man chased Torgerson, but lost him around the intersection of McKinley and Franklin streets. The backpack included clothing, as well as debit and credit cards, the man said. The debit and credit cards were destroyed, the man told police.
Two officers found Torgerson walking southbound on Cherry Street near Holmes Street and one put Torgerson into a “seated position.” Torgerson refused to identify himself, so an officer attempted to handcuff him. Torgerson resisted and backed away.
After police arrested Torgerson, he requested medical attention and was transported to Mercy Hospital. At the hospital, he screamed and called both officers and medical staff “many derogatory names,” and was “belligerant until he was escorted into a chair in a hospital room.”
An officer reported that Torgerson told him, “If I see you in any weight room, I promise you I’ll wrestle you to the ground.” The officer added Torgerson denied threatening him and said, “Did I say I’d shoot him in the face? That’s a threat.”
According to the complaint, the unidentified man had a “large” swollen cheek and was bleeding.
Torgerson faceds charges of misdemeanor battery, disorderly conduct, criminal damage to property, obstructing an officer and threatening police.
